question: The planes $x+y+z=1$ and $x-y+z=3$ intersect in a line. Obtain the vector equation of their line of intersection and hence determine the acute angle made by this line with the plane $2x+y+z=5$.
explanation:
Formation of the Line of Intersection
The equations of the first two planes are
$$x+y+z=1$$
and
$$x-y+z=3$$
Subtracting the first equation from the second gives
$$-2y=2$$
Hence,
$$y=-1$$
Substituting in $x+y+z=1$ gives
$$x+z=2$$
Let $x=\lambda$. Then $z=2-\lambda$. Thus, a general point of the line is
$$\left(\lambda,-1,2-\lambda\right)$$
Therefore, the vector equation of the line of intersection is
$$\vec{r}=(-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$$
Hence, a direction vector of the line is
$$\vec{b}=\hat{i}-\hat{k}$$

Angle with the Third Plane
A normal vector to the plane $2x+y+z=5$ is
$$\vec{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$$
If $\phi$ is the acute angle between the line and this plane, then
$$\sin\phi=\frac{|\vec{b}\cdot\vec{n}|}{|\vec{b}||\vec{n}|}$$
Now,
$$\vec{b}\cdot\vec{n}=1(2)+0(1)+(-1)(1)=1$$
Also,
$$|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{2},\quad |\vec{n}|=\sqrt{6}$$
Therefore,
$$\sin\phi=\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}$$
Hence,
$$\phi=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\right)$$

Final Result
The vector equation of the line of intersection is $\vec{r}=(-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$, and the acute angle made by this line with the plane $2x+y+z=5$ is $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\right)$.

options.A: $\vec r=(-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i-\hat k)$; acute angle with $2x+y+z=5$ is $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\right)$
options.B: $\vec r=(\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i+\hat k)$; acute angle is $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\right)$
options.C: $\vec r=(-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i-\hat k)$; acute angle is $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\right)$
options.D: $\vec r=(-\hat j+2\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i+\hat k)$; acute angle is $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\right)$
